description: Four-panel composite figure (all four panels are line plots of lattice strain versus applied strain measured by HEXRD on a low-density medium-Mn steel). (a) RD sample and (b) TD sample plot "Lattice Strain" (y, 0.0-0.6) against "Engineering Strain (%)" (x, 1.5-3.5 in (a), 1.5-4.0 in (b)) for nine individual reflections: FCC(111), FCC(200), FCC(220), FCC(311), FCC(222) drawn in grey open symbols and BCC(110), BCC(200), BCC(211), BCC(220) in red filled symbols. In both panels BCC(110) rises fastest (approaching the 0.6 gridline in (a) near 3.5% and ~0.55 in (b) near 4.0%), while FCC(311) and FCC(222) remain lowest and bend over around 2.5-3.0%. (c) RD and (d) TD show the weighted average lattice strain ("Average Lattice Strain", y 0.00-0.30) of FCC (open circles) and BCC (red filled circles), with dashed lines extending the initial linear slope. Arrows mark the deviation from linearity: epsilon=1.8% (FCC, black arrow) versus epsilon=2.3% (BCC, red arrow) in (c), and epsilon=2.1% (FCC) versus epsilon=2.9% (BCC) in (d). The figure demonstrates that austenite (FCC) yields first in both loading directions and that its average lattice strain peaks then declines, indicating strain partitioning and stress relaxation in austenite.

subfigures.description: Line plot for the RD sample: Lattice Strain (0.0-0.6) versus Engineering Strain (%) (1.5-3.5), with nine curves — FCC(111), FCC(200), FCC(220), FCC(311), FCC(222) as grey open symbols and BCC(110), BCC(200), BCC(211), BCC(220) as red filled symbols. BCC(110) is by far the steepest, approaching 0.6; FCC(311) and FCC(222) stay below ~0.1.

Same axes for the TD sample over Engineering Strain 1.5-4.0%. BCC(110) rises fastest to just above 0.5 near 4.0%; the remaining BCC and FCC curves cluster between ~0.1 and ~0.29, with the FCC curves flattening around 2.5-3.0%.

RD weighted average lattice strain (y 0.00-0.30) versus Engineering Strain (%) (1.5-3.5) for FCC (open circles) and BCC (red filled circles), each with a dashed extrapolation of the initial linear slope. Annotations: black arrow epsilon=1.8% (FCC) and red arrow epsilon=2.3% (BCC) mark the onset of deviation from linearity. FCC peaks near 0.11 and then decreases; BCC keeps rising to ~0.29.

TD weighted average lattice strain versus Engineering Strain (%) (1.5-4.0) for FCC and BCC with dashed linear extrapolations. Annotations: black arrow epsilon=2.1% (FCC) and red arrow epsilon=2.9% (BCC). FCC peaks near 0.13 around 3.2% then declines; BCC rises monotonically to ~0.28.

observations.observation: Panel (a) displays nine lattice-strain curves for the RD sample, labelled FCC(111), FCC(200), FCC(220), FCC(311), FCC(222) (grey open symbols) and BCC(110), BCC(200), BCC(211), BCC(220) (red filled symbols), plotted as Lattice Strain (0.0-0.6) versus Engineering Strain (%) (1.5-3.5).
In panel (a) the BCC(110) curve is the steepest and approaches the 0.6 lattice-strain gridline by 3.5% engineering strain, whereas FCC(311) and FCC(222) remain below 0.10 over the whole range.

In panel (b) (TD sample, Engineering Strain 1.5-4.0%) BCC(110) again rises fastest, reaching just above the 0.5 gridline near 4.0% strain, while the FCC curves level off around 2.5-3.0% at values between about 0.1 and 0.28.

Panels (c) and (d) plot the weighted average lattice strain (Average Lattice Strain, 0.00-0.30) of FCC (open circles) and BCC (red filled circles) against engineering strain, each accompanied by a dashed line extending the initial linear slope.

Printed annotations mark the deviation from linearity: epsilon=2.3% (red arrow, BCC) and epsilon=1.8% (black arrow, FCC) in panel (c), and epsilon=2.9% (red arrow, BCC) and epsilon=2.1% (black arrow, FCC) in panel (d).
In panel (c) the FCC average lattice strain peaks slightly above 0.10 between roughly 2.6% and 2.8% strain and then decreases, while the BCC average continues to rise to about 0.29 at 3.5%.
In panel (d) the FCC average lattice strain peaks near 0.13 at about 3.2% strain and then falls, while the BCC average rises monotonically to about 0.28 at 4.0%.
The caption states that the arrows indicate the starting point at which the curve deviates from linearity.

The citing text states that the weighted average lattice strain of austenite shows a change in slope at 1.8% applied strain for the RD sample and 2.1% for the TD sample, both smaller than the corresponding ferrite values (2.3% RD and 2.9% TD).
The citing text states that five austenite reflections (gamma 111, gamma 200, gamma 220, gamma 311, gamma 222) and four ferrite reflections (alpha 110, alpha 200, alpha 211, alpha 220) are presented.

The citing text reports that the lattice strain of all crystallographic planes in austenite shows an earlier change in slope than in ferrite, indicating earlier initiation of plastic deformation in austenite.
The citing text reports a slight reduction in austenite lattice strain after macroscopic yielding in both samples, interpreted as stress relaxation in the austenite.

The citing text states that pronounced strain partitioning between delta-ferrite and gamma+alpha aggregates is observed in the TD sample but not in the RD sample, with more strain concentrated in the gamma+alpha-prime mixed phase than in alpha-ferrite.

measured_quantities: strain at onset of deviation from linearity / plastic deformation (%)
